official.deadline_note: No central deadline exists: the governing date is the funding deadline specific to each course, published as a drop-down on the course page in the Postgraduate Course Directory. It is not the same as the course application deadline, and applicants must submit by whichever deadline is earlier.
official.application_cycle: 2027/28 cycle - the Trust's scholarship search currently lists scholarships for courses starting in the 2027/28 academic year
official.status_note: Applications for admission open in early September and applicants must submit by their course funding deadline for 2027/28 entry. The Trust's awarding period runs from mid-February to the end of July, with most awards made in February and March and unclaimed awards reallocated through the period.

The award covers the University tuition fee at the international rate, annual maintenance sufficient for a single person, the student visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge, plus various additional benefits.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Trust's flagship full-cost award for applicants from outside the UK and Ireland who are top-ranked by their prospective Cambridge department, paying international-rate tuition, single-person annual maintenance, the student visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge, with further benefits named in each award letter. Unlike most Trust scholarships, selection is on academic merit alone, so your finances do not count against you - but you must still fill in the funding section and hit your course's funding deadline, which is earlier than the application deadline and varies by course. Nothing is applied for separately: your single Cambridge admissions application is the whole entry.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-ranked applicants from outside the UK and Ireland targeting a funded MPhil, MASt, LLM, MRes, MPhil+PhD or PhD place at Cambridge who can meet their course's funding deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Look up your exact course page in the Postgraduate Course Directory and note the funding deadline drop-down - treat that date, not the application deadline, as your real cutoff
Draft the admissions application so it is complete, in English and in Latin script, well before that date; courses can reach capacity and close early
Brief your two referees so their references land in the Referee Portal by the same deadline
Complete the funding section and gather income evidence (salaries, business profit, rents, dividends) even though finances do not affect selection for this award
Confirm your course is a funded level (MPhil, MASt, LLM, MCL, MAcc, MRes, MEd, MCEP, MLitt, MPhil+PhD, MRes+PhD or PhD) and not an MBA, MFin, MSt, PGDip or other excluded premium level
Check you do not already hold a degree at or above the level you are applying for
common_rejection_risks: Missing the course funding deadline - this is the single fastest way to lose consideration for the majority of University funds
Failing to tick the funding section of the admissions form; without it the Trust cannot consider you at all
Not being ranked highly enough by your prospective department - ranking is decided by admissions, and the Trust can neither see nor influence it
Applying for an unfunded level such as the MBA, MFin, MSt, MV, AdvDip, BusD, EMBA, Global EMBA, PGCert or PGDip
Holding a degree at or above the level applied for, with the narrow exception of a required second MPhil before a PhD
Applying from the UK or Ireland, or being part-way through a Cambridge course without moving up a degree level
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published value covers only a single person's maintenance, so dependants' costs are uncovered; travel to the UK is not among the listed benefits; the University application fee is not covered (the Trust states it cannot help with application fees, including waivers); and any costs beyond the international-rate tuition fee for your course are yours to fund.
document_audit: References are not optional and must arrive via the Referee Portal by the same deadline - a late referee silently weakens you
The whole application must be in English and Latin script, including people and institution names
You need a separate application and separate supporting documents for each course you apply to
Applications submitted through agents are rejected - you must submit it yourself
You cannot add information once the application is submitted; anything extra can only be uploaded to your self-service account and is not essential
The funding section asks for income from all sources even though financial need is not a selection criterion here
alerts: The funding deadline is course-specific, earlier than the application deadline, and missing it removes you from most University funds

The Trust awarding window runs mid-February to the end of July, and unclaimed awards are reallocated until then - silence until the end of July means unsuccessful, and no feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants
For this award your financial situation does not affect selection, but you still complete the funding section, which feeds the other Trust scholarships you are eligible for
The Trust plays no part in admissions or College selection, cannot discuss your departmental ranking, cannot find you a supervisor and cannot help with application fees
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One application does everything: submit the admissions application through the University Applicant Portal with the funding section completed by your course funding deadline; referees upload references by the same date; departments rank applicants; the Trust then awards from mid-February to end of July against conditional offers.
